title: Look Before You Access: Efficient Heap Memory Safety for Embedded Systems on ARMv8-M
problem: Embedded firmware written in C/C++ is vulnerable to spatial memory vulnerabilities like buffer overflows that enable software attacks. Existing memory safety defenses introduce significant performance and memory overhead, making them impractical for resource-constrained embedded systems.
motivation: Efficient memory safety mechanisms are needed for embedded systems to defend against buffer overflow attacks without prohibitive overhead.
method: The paper introduces micro-fat pointer, which uses TT instructions—specialized hardware in ARMv8-M processors that check memory bounds—to catch buffer overflows efficiently. Each pointer carries metadata (extra information) describing where memory access is allowed; when memory is accessed, a TT instruction checks that the access respects these boundaries. By combining metadata with hardware support, the method achieves safety without the excessive performance or memory overhead of previous approaches, making it practical for embedded systems with limited resources.
key_novelty: Using TT instructions (a new hardware feature in ARMv8-M for checking memory bounds) to enable efficient fat pointer bounds-checking for heap memory in embedded systems.
contributions: Introduces micro-fat pointer architecture for practical heap memory safety on embedded systems
Exploits ARMv8-M TT instructions for efficient bounds-checking with minimal overhead
Achieves 41% performance improvement over existing heap memory safety solutions
Demonstrates applicability for embedded firmware protection against spatial attacks
primary_theme: Efficient heap memory safety for embedded systems
